questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go to the UK and Bristol had some interesting courses.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy, lots of information through email and the Bristol Uni app (instructions to download are in an email if I remember correctly)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Key handover, introduction course with other exchange students etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
It was easy enough through Bristol's websites and accommodation portal.  Most accoms are off campus. I'd recommend Clifton Hill House or Richmond Terrace (I didn't stay there but heard good things about them).
Had a Canadian friend who stayed in Metal Works and her entire flat was exchange students, which was cool. It was more modern/renovated too, but not as close to campus.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's expensive

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Main problem was the price

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There's a physical process you have to sign up for through one of their portals, I forget which one but you can't really miss it.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Before leaving it's all digital, all quite easy and super easy to mail about any questions etc. When you arrive there's a physical meeting where you register with staff

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A study abroad office with email and phone number, also regular uni offers. A lot like KU

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Only missed out on one beause I wasn't qualified for it, but they let you know quickly and offer alternatives. Ended up enjoying all the courses I took.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just remember to check/read your emails and you'll be good

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The readings were similar level to Copenhagen, but the exam essays were much shorter in length.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was more interactive

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Public Opinion & Democracy,
The politics of human rights,
Global justice

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Politics of human rights was really good

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
I lived near campus (15 min walk) so all my travel costs were going to London mostly (flixbus or national express is cheapest, around 50kr of you buy in advance). 

Housing was very expensive.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Lots of societes. They cost money though so I didn't join. But I got invited to some events by the fashion society through a friend. Free activities were also available to exchange students. Some there's limited spots you have to sign up for, it's on their website.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Fashion society was cool from my perspective. The exchange events and parties. Otherwise it was mostly with friends you went out.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
London but I stayed with friends, might be expensive if that's not an option. 
West Village Cafe in Clifton was worth the walk up the hill. Rova is a magazine shop that's got some cool finds. Loco Club by the train station was cool. Jazz nights at Gin & Juice. (All in Bristol)

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy, weather was bad even for England though. Rain + wind from the Atlantic made umbrellas impossible.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sit by people in seminars (holdundervisning basically). There's a student union too.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Bristol is a very leftist/political space which I appreciated

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
It's basically as expensive as London,
Sign up for activities, 
Don't stress

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: TK maxx is good for cheap furniture/decor. 2nd hand shops near campus take donations for when you leave.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting people from all over. Bristol had lots of exchange students.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a good Shawarma spot

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Can't think of anything

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
